Personality: Masinissa, a prominent figure of the Massyli, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Masinissa owes allegiance to the Mediterranean League, hailing from the noble house of Massyli. Historical Record: Masinissa, son of King Gaia of the Massylii, raised partly at Carthage, a young man of tireless strength and a born horseman. He hopes to win glory leading Numidian horse for Carthage, and dreams of one day uniting all Numidia under his own rule. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
